summary: postcss-semantic-themes ships obfuscated import-time loader and VM-detection native addon under cover of a CSS theme kit
details: Package is advertised as a zero-runtime CSS theme kit producing plain CSS custom properties, but the published tarball ships ~900KB of heavily obfuscated ESM loaders (cache-warm.mjs, cache-sweep.mjs, build-cache.mjs) plus workspaces.js, all using string-array + base64/XOR obfuscation and wiring to eval, child_process, spawn, exec, createRequire, and dynamic import() sinks. The ESM entry lib.mjs re-exports from tokens.mjs, whose top-level import pulls in cache-warm.mjs, so the obfuscated loader executes on consumer import of the package. The package also ships cross-platform native addons at native/{linux,darwin,win32}/{x64,arm64}/cache-probe.node whose exported symbols (VMDetect::GetCallback, vbox_module, qemu_fw_cfg, qemu_usb, qemu_virtual_dmi, smbios_vm_bit, hypervisor_dir, hypervisor_bit, dmidecode, dmesg, kmsg, pci_devices, bluestacks, amd_sev_msr, is_x86_process_on_arm) and a bundled LICENSE-node-vm-detect.txt identify the addon as a VM/sandbox-detection library. A CSS theme kit has no legitimate need for an import-time obfuscated process-spawning loader or a VM-detection native module; the combination is the hostile-dropper shape, with VM-detection used as anti-analysis to gate payload execution on real victim machines, and directly contradicts the package's own README.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
